The three sources converge on the same core position, with each contributing a distinct layer:

**Support FAQ (NL-006):** Scanned PDFs require OCR; without it the standard parser extracts zero text, making files unsearchable and citations impossible [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. OCR is heuristic: blurry or low-resolution scans, handwriting, and complex multi-column layouts cause misread characters and broken citations, knowledge gaps, and longer processing times [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. Recommended resolutions include verifying OCR is enabled, exporting a digital text-searchable PDF instead of scanning a printed sheet, and using the Advanced OCR Pipeline (Enterprise or Growth add-on) [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. Tables are garbled because OCR reads line-by-line across columns, so the FAQ recommends converting to CSV/XLSX or using clear dark grid lines [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. The standard OCR engine ignores handwriting and physical annotations, so such notes must be transcribed into digital text in a DOCX or Markdown file to be searchable [NL-006#NL-006-S03].

**Product guide (NL-002):** PDF is the default format and scanned/image-only PDFs require OCR processing, with page/paragraph citation precision for PDFs generally [NL-002#NL-002-S08]. It also documents ingestion queue capacity limits per plan (Growth: 200 documents parallel; Enterprise: up to 1,000 parallel threads), with overflow placed in a sequential ingestion buffer [NL-002#NL-002-S08].

**Customer interviews (NL-021, NL-024, NL-018, NL-017):** Ingestion/OCR issues are the single largest support category — 112 of 412 tickets (~27%) in May 2026 [NL-021#NL-021-S02]. Enterprise customers (e.g., BrightPath Healthcare, Northstar Financial) have 40–50% of files as scanned PDFs without a text layer; TutorChat either returns answers with no citations or citations pointing to the entire document, and CSAT dropped from 4.5 to 3.8 [NL-021#NL-021-S02]. The standard parser indexes a scan as one large metadata block, and current workarounds are to export native DOCX/text files or exclude scans from the active corpus [NL-024#NL-024-S04]. Deleted scans are immediately marked inactive and update visible within 5 minutes [NL-024#NL-024-S04]. In clinical settings, OCR failures caused omitted critical ventilator alarm thresholds [NL-018#NL-018-S05]. Manual OCR pre-processing is a severe labor bottleneck — ~12,000 pages requiring ~3 months of IT effort [NL-018#NL-018-S05] — and customers explicitly ask for the KnowledgeHub to do OCR automatically rather than requiring external tools [NL-017#NL-017-S06]. All customer accounts point to the Advanced OCR ingestion pipeline, targeted for August 2026 release, as the awaited fix [NL-024#NL-024-S04][NL-018#NL-018-S05][NL-017#NL-017-S06].

**Collective takeaway:** All three sources agree that scanned/image-only PDFs are unprocessable without OCR, that OCR is error-prone on low-quality or layout-complex scans, that manual OCR is an unacceptable burden on customers, and that the near-term fix is using native text-based files while the Advanced OCR Pipeline (August 2026) is the planned automated solution.
